title: Tiger Woods makes first public appearance since DUI arrest in March
content:
HARTFORD, Conn. — Tiger Woods has returned to his position as the chairman of the PGA Tour’s Future Competition Committee, appearing publicly Tuesday for the first time since his DUI arrest less than three months ago.

He appeared alongside PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp, during a news conference at the Travelers Championship.

Woods helped Rolapp announce landmark changes to the schedule and competitive structure of the PGA Tour that will take effect in 2028, with the top 120 players each year competing on a “Championship Series” featuring 72-hole tournaments with a cut and at least $20 million divided among the field. It is the signature accomplishment of Rolapp’s nearly year-long tenure as CEO and was done with Woods’ support from the beginning.

After making a short introduction for Rolapp that included no mention of his absence, Woods left the stage. “I think I can speak for everyone in that we are happy to see you back,” Rolapp said.

When approached by The Athletic following the press conference, Woods said, “Not right now” and walked out of the room.

Woods had temporarily paused his chairman duties while he sought rehabilitation treatment at a facility in Switzerland, but now that he has returned to the U.S., he will resume his role, a PGA Tour spokesman said. Woods has been “hyper-involved” in boardroom conversations for the past several weeks, the spokesman said. Woods’ participation also included in-person appearances during Monday’s board meetings and a vote to move forward, eyeing Tuesday’s announcement.

Following his arrest on March 27 after a rollover two-vehicle crash near his home on Jupiter Island, Fla., Woods announced that he would be retreating from public life for an indeterminate period of time.

“I know and understand the seriousness of the situation I find myself in today. I am stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health. This is necessary in order for me to prioritize my well-being and work toward lasting recovery,” he said in a statement posted to his X account on March 31.

Woods was ultimately charged with a DUI, property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful urinalysis test after the incident. Police officers found two hydrocodone pills, a prescription painkiller, in his pocket. They also attested that Woods was “lethargic” and his eyes were bloodshot at the scene.

Woods still faces misdemeanor charges related to his DUI, after initially entering a not guilty plea with the Martin County Circuit Court. As of the latest court filing on June 18, discovery is still ongoing as it pertains to Woods’ case, and his next hearing has been rescheduled for Aug. 4.

Immediately after the arrest, the PGA Tour’s Future Competition Committee met virtually without Woods and advised that he would rejoin the committee when “he is ready to do so.” The group also stated that it was in full support of Woods’ effort to focus on his health and well-being. Woods also canceled his appearance at Augusta National Golf Club, where he was set to unveil his redesign of Augusta Municipal Golf Course, otherwise known as The Patch.

TMZ photographed Woods earlier this month leaving a private airport in Florida.
